mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for 3 months, or IC > 0.05 in a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous UNRATE AND PAYEMS > previous PAYEMS
failure_condition: IC < 0.1 over 60 days or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline in strengthening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates robust supply-side growth with muted demand pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 110.9 AND CPIAUCSL falls by > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day IC negative or 5-day returns negative despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the ratio of imports to exports (not directly observable in the given proxies) would typically be inferred through industrial production and employment, but here we proxy via a sustained drop in RSAFS (demand in dollars) while INDPRO continues rising, suggesting supply chain resilience that supports S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns negative with sustained INDPRO up and RSAFS down.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months in a tightening regime (as signaled by UNRATE > 6%), the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive despite policy conditions matching the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment suggests a labor market imbalance favoring demand, which can boost equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns flat or negative despite the spike.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 3% while the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) shows no acceleration suggests supply chain expansion outpacing demand, which can support equity valuations and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
A sustained decline in the 12-month moving average of FEDFUNDS below 3% triggers a risk-off spiral, lowering equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns positive contrary to the signal.
